entries.title: Silverglen - The Missing Unit 8? | Chatsworth From Above
entries.description:
Welcome to another episode of Chatsworth From Above! 🚁

We've travelled from Unit 1 all the way through to Unit 7...

But what happened to Unit 8? 👀

Chatsworth's numbered sequence famously skips Unit 8, and while Silverglen was never officially designated as Unit 8, for the purpose of our journey through Chatsworth, we're having a little fun and giving Silverglen that missing spot.

Welcome to SILVERGLEN — our unofficial Unit 8!

This episode takes us high above one of the most fascinating parts of the greater Chatsworth landscape.

Unlike the numbered units we've explored previously, Silverglen has a history and character of its own, with development in the area predating the formal establishment of Chatsworth's numbered housing scheme.

From its hills, valleys and residential areas to some remarkable landmarks, we explore the Silverglen of yesterday and the community we see from above today.

Among the places featured in this episode:

📍 Silverglen Nature Reserve    
📍 The former Odeon Cinema  
📍 SCDIFA Hall  
📍 The former Sol Namara Hotel  
📍 Silverglen's residential areas and surrounding landscape

We uncover the history behind some of these landmarks, including the Odeon Cinema, which opened in 1969; the story of SCDIFA and its roots stretching back to 1914; the Sol Namara Hotel; and the remarkable natural environment preserved within Silverglen Nature Reserve.

If you grew up in Silverglen or remember the area from years gone by, add your memories to the comments. Your stories help preserve pieces of local history that aren't always found in official records.

entries.title: How Harbour Pilots Leave Massive Ships at Sea | Durban Harbour
entries.description:
Have you ever wondered how a harbour pilot gets off a massive ship after guiding it out of port?

In this video, I captured a fascinating operation at the Port of Durban — a helicopter hovering above a departing vessel before lifting the harbour pilot from the ship.

Harbour pilots play a vital role in helping large vessels safely navigate into and out of busy ports. Their specialised local knowledge allows them to work alongside the ship's captain and bridge crew as vessels navigate the harbour and its approaches.

But the action doesn't stop there.

After witnessing the helicopter pilot transfer, we'll take a look at some of the incredible vessels I've captured entering and leaving Durban Harbour — from massive cargo vessels and car carriers to impressive cruise ships.

Durban Harbour is constantly moving, and sometimes the most interesting operations are happening right in front of us without most people knowing what they're watching.

If you enjoy seeing Durban, our coastline and places around South Africa from a different perspective, subscribe to Juelz T for more.

entries.title: Unit 7 Montford | Chatsworth From Above Ep. 7
entries.description:
Welcome to Episode 7 of Chatsworth From Above.

Today, our journey takes us over Unit 7, Montford.

From ground level, Montford is a maze of familiar numbered roads, homes, schools, shops and community spaces. But from above, you begin to see how it all comes together across the hills of Unit 7.

In this episode, we explore Montford's distinctive landscape, the story behind its name, its famous 700-series roads, schools, shopping centre, sporting and recreational spaces, community facilities and the way the neighbourhood has changed over the decades.

One of the most interesting features of Montford is its numbered-road network. Road 701, Road 706, Road 719, Road 721, Road 723, Road 733, Road 736, Road 748 and many others have become part of the identity of Unit 7.

And then there's Road 706...
It has to be one of the longest numbered roads in Chatsworth – but is it actually THE longest?

I couldn't find an authoritative municipal record confirming it, so I'm putting that question to the people who know Chatsworth best.
Do you know the answer?

Another important landmark in this episode is Montford Shopping Centre. For generations, this has been part of everyday life in Unit 7. Long before today's enormous malls and online shopping, local centres like this were home to family-run grocery stores, butchers, bakeries, takeaways, pharmacies, hairdressers, hardware stores, medical services and many other businesses. Some remain.
Others exist only in the memories of the people who grew up here.

Education is another major part of Montford's landscape, with schools including Montford Primary, Seven Hills Primary, Tyburn Primary, AYS Memorial Primary, Montarena Secondary, Brindhavan Secondary, Meadowlands Technical High and Welbedene Secondary serving generations of families from the area.

We also take a look at Montford's sporting and recreational spaces, community facilities, places of worship and the changing residential landscape visible from above.

🏠 Houses have expanded.
🛣️ Roads have become busier.
🏪 Businesses have changed.
🏫 Generations have passed through the area's schools.

But Unit 7 remains Montford.

And now I want to hear from the people who actually know this community.
Which road did you grow up on?
Which school did you attend?
Which old Montford shops and businesses do you remember?
Which sporting clubs or community landmarks should never be forgotten?
And what existed in the old Montford that has completely disappeared today?

Most importantly, if you've moved away from Montford, what is the first memory that comes back when you see Unit 7 from above?

Add your memories to the comments and help us preserve another piece of Chatsworth's history.

entries.title: A Whale Washed Ashore at uMhlanga Lighthouse | August 2023
entries.description:
A sobering sight unfolded at uMhlanga Beach on Wednesday, 16 August 2023, when the carcass of a juvenile whale washed ashore roughly 200 metres south of the iconic uMhlanga Lighthouse.

In this video, we look back at the moment that drew crowds to the beachfront and the reminder it gave us of the vast, vulnerable world that exists just beyond our shoreline.

While contemporary reports described the whale as juvenile, there was no reliable public confirmation of its species or cause of death. This video keeps the story factual and honours the animal without speculating.

ISIPINGO RIVER MOUTH BREACHES! 🌊 Floodwaters Rush Into the Ocean | Durban Flooding
entries.description:
Heavy rainfall across Durban has caused water levels in the Isipingo River to rise dramatically, prompting an emergency intervention at the Isipingo Beach river mouth.

Following concerns about flooding in surrounding low-lying areas, eThekwini Municipality used machinery to lower and remove sand at the mouth, creating a channel for the accumulated river water to escape into the Indian Ocean.

In this video, I take you right to the Isipingo River mouth to show what is happening. The river is now flowing strongly into the ocean but what makes this footage particularly interesting is watching the breach actively widen. As the water rushes through the opening, it erodes the sandy sides of the channel, causing sections to collapse into the water.

Nearby, the effects of the rising water levels are already clearly visible. A local soccer ground is flooded, while water around the vegetation has risen remarkably high beneath the hanging bird nests.

This footage was captured on 18 September 2026 and documents conditions at the time of filming.

With continued rainfall and flooding affecting parts of Durban, please exercise extreme caution around rivers, flooded roads, low-lying bridges and fast-moving water.

entries.title: Durban You Never See | Inside Durban Harbour From Above
entries.description:
There is a side of Durban that most people never get to see.

Captured from above in 2022, this journey begins over the Bluff before moving towards the entrance of Durban Harbour, the Millennium Tower and South Pier.

We then fly deeper into one of South Africa’s most important ports, passing cargo ships, dry-bulk operations, industrial storage tanks and the extensive Island View terminal area.

A full 360-degree aerial view reveals how the harbour, Bluff, Indian Ocean and city all connect. Later, we explore the back of the port around Bayhead and Grunter Gully—an industrial landscape hidden from most residents and visitors.

This is more than a beautiful aerial view. It is a closer look at the working side of Durban and the infrastructure helping connect South Africa to the rest of the world.
